articleTitle: Fast Spectral Clustering Based on Fusion Density Peaks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: In recent years, Spectral Clustering and its variants have attracted much attention due to their excellent clustering performance. These algorithms first build a graph on the data based on local similarity, then compute the spectral decomposition of the Laplacian matrix of the graph, and finally achieve clustering by performing K-Means on embeddings obtained from spectral decomposition. However, the traditional spectral clustering method is difficult to deal with large-scale datasets. The large size of data will make the spectral decomposition slow and consume a lot of computational resources. To solve these problem, this paper first proposes a clustering algorithm named FGDPSC. FGDP-SC identifies global density peak points of the data as anchors in multi-scales defined by near-field, mid-field, and farfield, characterizes the data using a bipartite graph with anchors, and performs clustering efficiently through the transfer-cut of the bipartite graph. Experiments on real-world data validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, especially on largescale data, by outperforming the classical Spectral Clustering algorithm and its main variants.

articleTitle: A Lightweight GNN-Based Graph Embedding Method for Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Knowledge graph is a graphical knowledge base for organizing and representing knowledge. In knowledge graph, each piece of knowledge is represented as a triplet form of (head entity, relation, tail entity). The main idea of graph embedding based on graph neural networks is to project the entities and relations in the knowledge graph into a low-dimensional space for various downstream tasks. However, existing GNN-based knowledge graph embedding methods suffer from the problem of excessive number of parameters. To solve the problem, we propose a lightweight GNN-based knowledge graph embedding method. Lightweight entity feature vectors are obtained by splicing entities and relations. We validate the effectiveness of our method on a link prediction task. Comparisons are made with three different baseline methods on two real-world datasets Kinship and UMLS. The results show that our embedding method reduces the number of parameters in the model without loss of accuracy.

articleTitle: ADS-B Radiation Source Signal Identification Based on Deep Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: ADS-B (Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast) radiated source signals have a crucial position in aviation communications, and their identification and analysis are essential to ensure air transportation safety. However, the performance of traditional radiated source signal recognition techniques needs to be improved, and the recognition model combined with deep learning has achieved better recognition performance but faces the problem of decreasing recognition accuracy under a low signal-to-noise ratio environment. To address this problem, this paper designs a new deep residual network (DRN) to improve the recognition accuracy. Through the special construction of the residual structure, the depth of the network can be increased losslessly so that the model learns deeper features of the data. In addition, a preprocessing method of phase solving is adopted to test the model’s ability to recognize fake messages through the fake ICAO bit substitution for “Fake Message” experiments. The experimental results show that the DRN model still has a recognition accuracy of 85.68% in the face of fake messages, which is a good ability to recognize fake messages. Under the low signal-to-noise ratio of 3db, the DRN model still has a recognition accuracy of 95.64%, which is 24.02% higher than that of the convolutional neural network model.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Polar Codes in Small IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Error-correction in the communication module of IoT systems is a mission-critical task. The Polar code is one of the modern 5G wireless technologies. Most conventional decoding methods are iterative. It is interesting to investigate the feasibility of AI methodology, such as machine learning, for small Polar codes. In this paper, we design a small artificial neural network for this purpose. It is shown that this neural network can successfully decode four small Polar codes: both non-systematic and systematic, with codeword length 8 and 16, respectively.

articleTitle: Visual Analysis of Key Core Technologies Research Hotspots and Trends Based on CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This article reviews 564 articles on China National Knowledge Infrastructure and 1551 articles on Web of Science from 2002 to 2024 under the theme of Key Core Technologies. Using CiteSpace bibliometric analysis software, the keywords, authors, and institutions of Chinese and foreign literature are visualized and analyzed, summarizing the current research status of key core technologies and assessing future research trends. The research results indicate that the hot topics in domestic and foreign literature are focused on the classification of key core technologies, the application of key core technologies in industrial transformation and upgrading, and path breakthroughs. The core technological breakthroughs in areas such as digital transformation, artificial intelligence, and big data in the future will be a key research topic in related fields.

articleTitle: The Impact of Personalized Social Media Advertising on Consumers’ Willingness to Click
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This study mainly studies the application of artificial intelligence personalized recommendation system in social media platforms. The study was verified by the partial least squares method (PSL-SEM). The partial least squares method is mainly estimated through a series of iterative algorithms, based on the original data, to find out the linear relationship among each latent variable and its related latent variables. In order to ensure the validity of the evidence, the data were cleaned after the questionnaire was collected to ensure the credibility of the results. The results show that personalized social media advertising consistency and social ability have a positive effect on consumers’ click willingness; psychological resistance has mediated the relationship between consistency and social and advertising click willingness.

articleTitle: Explicit Feature Pyramids Are Enhanced Object Detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Object detection has seen new advancements with the introduction of DETR, leading to notable performance improvements. However, DETR-based object detectors, such as AdaMixer and Sparse-RCNN, suffer from long training times and defective accuracy for small objects due to their complex heads. Previous attempts to address the issues by using dense priors for initialization and single-decoder layer detectors have resulted in lower accuracy compared to those with complex decoder layers. To enhance multi-scale information capture, the traditional object detection methods use Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN). In this study, we present an Optimal Transport Decoder (OTD), a pioneering effort in employing patches as its fundamental units to investigate the feature pyramid structure for the research-hot DETR, deviating from the traditional grid prediction method. OTD proposes an explicit feature pyramid between the backbone and decoder, which can enhance multi-scale image representation without increasing computational complexity. A box distribution alignment method is designed to leverage Optimal Transport (OT) for calculating the model’s loss so as to converge towards the global optimum instead of the local optima, even when dealing with intricate scenes and small target detection. The experimental results verify our model OTD over-performing the state-of-the-art related models.

articleTitle: Significance of Feature Importance on Crop Prediction Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This study introduces an approach to advancing sustainable agriculture through the application of Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques, leveraging the Crop Recommender Dataset with Soil Nutrition. Aimed at optimizing crop yields while minimizing environmental impacts, the research employs a comprehensive analysis of soil nutrients, underscoring the pivotal role these elements play in agricultural productivity. By integrating advanced ML and DL models, including Gradient Boosting, Multilayer Perceptron, and 1D Convolutional Neural Networks, parameters are fine-tuned to achieve unprecedented prediction accuracy. Through a detailed feature importance analysis, key soil nutrients critical in influencing crop yield predictions are identified. Results showcase exceptional performance with 1D-CNN obtaining a high AUC score of $99.45 \%$ followed by XGBoost with the original dataset and after feature reduction, SVM and 1D-CNN models achieved a high AUC score of $99.58 \%$ and $99.51 \%$, respectively. This paper contributes significant insights towards implementing efficient and sustainable farming practices, showcasing the potential of AI in revolutionizing precision agriculture. Findings not only pave the way for enhancing agricultural productivity but also for reducing environmental degradation, marking a step forward in the journey towards sustainable farming methodologies.

articleTitle: An Elevator Advertisement Recommendation System Design based on Machine Vision and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: In recent years, machine vision sensors have been continuously developed and gradually applied to advertising industry for accurate advertisement recommendation. However, because of the isolated environment, it is very difficult to recommend advertisement in elevator cages. In this study, a novel advertisement recommendation system is designed for the elevator, based on machine vision sensors, Raspberry Pi, deep learning neural networks, information management system, and socket communication, which are employed to analyze the features of the passengers in the elevators and recommend the most suitable advertisements for them. This system aims to help advertisers improve the effect of advertising activities. The simulation results show that the proposed system in this paper has a very accurate performance and can be widely applied in the elevators.

articleTitle: Wheat Pest Identification Based on Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: In recent years, effective pest management has become of cross-application of artificial intelligence and big data technologies in agriculture and environment. Nowadays, plant pests have just become a serious problem, which affects the ecological health as well as the growth of crops. In order to further better target traditional crop wheat for pest management, this study utilizes advanced deep learning techniques to accurately detect and categorize common wheat pests (“wireworm”, “Beet spot flies”, and “Cicadellidae”). Through the comparative analysis with the baseline model ResNet-18 model, this study also introduces the more advanced models SE-RegNetY and SEInception-ResNet-V3 models for pest identification in previous studies. Notably, among the three models applied in this study, the SE-Inception-ResNet-V3 model showed excellent results, achieving a significant average overall accuracy of $81.50 \%$ and kappa coefficient of $72.24 \%$, which were $10.3 \%$ and nearly $14.8 \%$ higher than the results of the benchmark ResNet-18 model, respectively. This study marks a further application of deep learning and artificial intelligence in agricultural pest management. By improving the accuracy of agricultural pest identification and classification, it provides the basis and foundation for more sustainable and environmentally friendly pest control methods.

articleTitle: Pioneering Testing and Assessment Framework For AI-Powered SAR ATR Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Recent advancements in machine learning and deep learning techniques have significantly enhanced the performance of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Automatic Target Recognition (ATR). However, the inherent opacity and uncertainty of AI pose challenges, as there is a lack of systematic testing and standardized metrics for evaluating AI-based SAR ATR systems. It hinders the application of SAR ATR system in safety-critical domains. In this paper, we present testing and assessment framework for AI-based SAR ATR system inspired recent developed AI-system testing and standard. We further present the level-1 and level 2 metrics to assess the SAR-ATR systems. It does not involve that algorithm recognition performance but the whole software system quality in the perspective of software engineering. Throughout testing and assessment for the whole system, it fosters application of the AI-based SAR ATR system in practice.

articleTitle: An Approach for Detecting AIGC Text Hallucinations Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This paper presents an approach for detecting AIGC(Artificial Intelligence Generated Content) text hallucinations based on a knowledge graph framework. Comparison algorithms are utilized to analyze text data and extract key features, which are mapped onto the knowledge graph for comprehensive analysis. By innovating the Jaccard Index formula, KGDH Jaccard Index formula is proposed to demonstrate the index of text hallucination generation. Through empirical evaluations and comparisons, the effectiveness and feasibility of this approach in identifying text hallucinations is demonstrated. This research contributes to the field of AI ethics and misinformation detection by providing a systematic framework for scrutinizing the credibility of AI-generated content.

articleTitle: Adversarial Adaptive Stance Detection Model for International Media Portrait Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: International public opinion mainly refers to the opinions and attitudes expressed by international media on a certain event through news coverage, primarily conveyed and disseminated through news texts. In a complex and ever-changing public opinion environment, international media play a crucial role. Media profiling aims to describe the characteristics and evolutionary trends of public opinion for a specific media outlet or group of media outlets by analyzing the themes, emotions, and language styles of their news releases. This paper, set against the backdrop of the COVID-19 pandemic, collects news data related to the COVID-19 epidemic from the Google News Database and constructs an international public opinion database on the COVID-19 epidemic. Based on transfer learning and adversarial learning theories, an adversarial adaptation stance detection model is proposed to enhance the model’s generalization ability while ensuring the effectiveness of stance detection. Using this adversarial adaptation stance detection model, international public opinion data on the COVID-19 epidemic were analyzed, and a portrait of international mainstream media during the COVID-19 epidemic was constructed and thoroughly analyzed.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Coordination Network Algorithm Based on AdaDelta and Its Gym Environment Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a bidirectional coordination network algorithm based on AdaDelta and implements the StarCraft research environment based on the openAI gym interface specification. Unlike traditional bidirectional coordination network algorithms that use random gradient descent strategies, this paper adopts AdaDelta to optimize actor and critical networks, and compares and analyzes the different key parameters in the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, as well as the impact of Gaussian noise on winning rate and convergence speed. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has a higher winning rate and faster convergence speed compared to the traditional BiCNet algorithm.

articleTitle: Utilizing Clinical and Genetic Markers to Estimate Neonatal Exposure to Maternal Smoking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Maternal smoking during pregnancy is a significant public health concern that negatively affects fetal development, leading to complications such as low birth weight and increased risk of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) and affecting crucial biological processes. Cord blood cotinine, a biomarker of nicotine exposure, serves as a reliable indicator of fetal exposure to tobacco smoke, including secondhand and thirdhand smoke. My research develops a machine learning framework that combines clinical and genetic markers to predict neonatal cord blood cotinine levels, a biomarker of tobacco smoke exposure, in the absence of prior information about maternal smoking. The framework utilizes a dataset comprised of clinical and genomic information from cord blood, maternal blood, and placental samples, sourced from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) platform. Four machine learning algorithms-K-Nearest Neighbor, Multi-Layer Perceptron, XGBoost, and Random Forest-were employed in the framework’s training and testing phases. XGBoost emerged as the most effective algorithm, achieving the best overall performance across four evaluation metrics (RMSE $=20.92$, MAE $=8.79$, MAPE $\left.=9.89, R^{2}=0.31\right)$. The results underscore the potential of this methodology in accurately predicting cord blood cotinine levels, thereby facilitating the identification of tobacco exposure in neonates and enabling the implementation of targeted health interventions to mitigate associated risks.

articleTitle: Study on the Rainfall-flood Association Pattern Database Based on Image Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Precipitation images can clearly reflect the rainfall spatio-temporal features and play an important role in hydrological analysis and flood forecasting. However, it is challenging to mine the association response relationship between rainfall and flood events. This paper proposed a rainfall-flood association pattern database construction method based on rainfall image features. First, the rainfall pattern database and flood pattern database are constructed respectively through the steps of hydrological process segmentation, feature extraction, similarity measurement and cluster analysis. Additionally, association rule mining algorithm is used to conduct rainfall-flood association pattern mining and consrtuct the rainfall-flood association pattern database. The experimental results in the Jialing River basin show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively mine the rainfall-flood association pattern database and provide technical support for intelligent flood prediction based on historical scene patterns.

articleTitle: Random variate generation for discrete fuzzy numbers based on α-cuts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Probabilistic based random variate generation is the most popular method for representing randomness into simulation scenarios that could occur in real life. The main idea behind the use of random numbers to replicate the value of a uncertain variable can also be extended to fuzzy sets, including discrete fuzzy sets. This way, it is possible to use random numbers and the $\alpha$-cut of a discrete fuzzy set to retrieve a random variate alongside its membership degree. To do so, a method for computing discrete fuzzy random variates based on $\alpha$-cuts is proposed and applied to two examples: a comprehensive and a simulation example.

articleTitle: A Fast Sorting and Recognition Method Based on Multi-Domain Parameter for Sar Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), as a high-resolution imaging device, is widely used in battlefield reconnaissance. In order to disrupt the imaging effect of SAR, jamming SAR has become the primary method of adversarial reconnaissance. The prerequisite for interfering with SAR is to identify the SAR signal. The characteristics of full pulse data (FPD) and intermediate frequency data (IMD) of SAR signals are analyzed in this article. The multi-domain parameters is consisted by these characteristics. Moreover, a method based on multi-domain parameters is proposed to fast sorting and identify the SAR signal. The proposed method can quickly sort and recognize SAR signals from massive data. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis Using Cross Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Aspect-level sentiment analysis is a challenging task that involves classifying emotions towards specific aspects mentioned in a sentence. Despite notable progress in previous research, this task remains highly complex. The key focus is on effectively encoding semantics and capturing the interaction between aspect items and context. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel sentiment classification method called ALSA-CA. By leveraging the BERT model for semantic encoding and incorporating a cross-attention mechanism to model aspect-item-context interactions, our approach demonstrates improved performance. Additionally, we introduce a positional weighting method that considers the relative positions of words and aspect items within sentences. Through extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method compared to current state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Research on the Relationship between Big Data Analytics Capabilities, Organizational Agility and Product Innovation Performance-The Moderating Role of Technological Intensity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Based on the dynamic capability theory, a theoretical model that big data analytics capabilities can promote product innovation performance by improving organizational agility under the adjustment of technological intensity is constructed. Smart PLS 4.0 software is used to conduct empirical analysis on the survey data of enterprises that have adopted big data analytics application practice. The results show that: ➀ Big data analytics capabilities have a significant positive impact on product innovation performance; ➁ Organizational agility plays a mediating role between big data analytics capabilities and product innovation performance; ➂ Technological intensity positively regulates the relationship between organizational agility and product innovation performance. This study explores the internal mechanism of big data analytics capabilities affecting product innovation, enriches the theoretical research on product innovation performance, and provides a theoretical basis for enterprises to promote product performance through digitalization.

articleTitle: Enhancing Arabic Audio Quality through Neural Network-Based Upscaling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The ubiquity of data and its capture methods play a pivotal role in information communication. With the advent of online platforms, organizations extensively use compression techniques to mitigate costs and reduce network traffic, often at the expense of audio quality. This paper addresses this challenge by utilising an approach to audio data upscaling through neural network. The method specifically targets the generation of missing high-frequency components, facilitating speech super-resolution and bandwidth expansion. A key distinction of this work is its focus on Arabic audio content, a domain that has seen limited exploration in the context of neural network-based audio enhancement. Along with the development and introduction of an Arabic audio dataset curated for the purposes of this study. Experimental results validate the efficacy of the proposed approach, demonstrating marked improvements in audio quality.

articleTitle: A Data-driven Model for NOx Prediction in a Cement Clinker Calcination System Based on a Robust ESN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Nitrogen oxide (NOx) is one of the important atmospheric pollutants released during Cement material calcination process. Due to the complex physical and chemical reactions and harsh calcination environment, it is a challenging task to predict the NOx concentration in a cement clinker calcination system. To address this problem, this paper design a prediction model based on a robust echo state network. To improve the robustness to noise, Cauchy loss function and a mixed penalty term are introduced. Meanwhile, a corresponding iterative algorithm is proposed to optimize the parameters of the proposed model. Finally, experimental results on real data show the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: A Vehicle Detection and Ranging Algorithm Based on Fast Mapping Statistics CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Vehicle detection and ranging play an important role in the assisted driving system in intelligent cars. In the process of automobile driving, by detecting and identifying the vehicle in front and calculating the distance between it and the vehicle in front, it can ensure a certain safety distance from the vehicle in front and greatly reduce traffic safety accidents. This paper presents a vehicle detection and ranging algorithm that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with fast mapping statistics and the binocular vision principle. This algorithm is built upon the advancements in deep learning techniques made in recent years, using labeled car sample data to train CNN to get the detector model, and using the test vehicle samples to detect the trained detector model and frame out the vehicle image, and then using binocular vision principle to frame out the vehicle image for ranging, and then using the binocular vision principle to determine the distance between the vehicle and the vehicle. Then the binocular vision principle is applied to the framed vehicle image for ranging to realize the effect of vehicle detection and ranging in front.

articleTitle: Cassandra vs. MongoDB: A Systematic Review of Two NoSQL Data Stores in Their Industry Uses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This paper analyzes two NoSQL data stores: the column-family data store with Cassandra as an example and the document-oriented data store using MongoDB as another example. By conducting a systematic review, this article examines the challenges and opportunities for the most recent industrial applications of these two data stores. As NoSQL data stores, both Cassandra and MongoDB are capable of processing live streaming data. In this systematic review, their applications in storing weather data, traffic data, radio spectrum data, live news data, and spatial data are discussed and compared.

articleTitle: Prediction of Energy Consumption of Supermarket Refrigeration Systems Using DMD and LSTM-NN Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The energy consumption of the refrigeration systems can account to over $20 \%$ of global electric energy consumption. It is crucial to optimal design and control of this kind of energy intensive system to improve its energy efficiency and thereby also contribute to climate protection. By focusing on a class of supermarket refrigeration systems, this work investigates how to use the emerging data-driven modeling methods, i.e. the Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) method and LSTM-NN method, to make a dynamic prediction of the energy consumption of these systems. The relevant data is produced from an industrial digital twin system. After analyzing and treating the original data, both the simple DMD modeling method and the sophisticated LSTM-NN method are applied to obtain a prediction model to forecast the compressors’ energy consumption subject to different ambient air temperature conditions. It has been observed that a single DMD model trained cannot perform well even for limited range, due to the nonlinearity inherent in the concerned systems. Thereby, the LSTM-NN model is applied for better prediction performance. After enhancing the standard LSTM-NN into an observer-type of LSTM-NN architecture (i.e., introducing output feedback into the standard LSTM-NN), the LSTM-NN model exhibits a precise prediction performance even with smaller set of training data, which indicates a promising potential to extend this type of solution into real-life industrial applications.

articleTitle: LongMuEL: An entity disambiguation method targeting multiple sources of data and long text
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Entity disambiguation is an important method for completing knowledge graphs. The data used for knowledge graph completion often integrates various data types and formats. When designing models for entity disambiguation, a key task is to design a knowledge fusion module to efficiently obtain embeddings of candidate entities from the descriptive text and structured data of the candidates. Since the length of candidate entity descriptive text usually far exceeds the limit of input text for pre-trained models, how to incorporate truncated text knowledge into the embeddings of candidate entities is also a problem to be considered when designing entity disambiguation models. In this paper, we propose a novel entity disambiguation model, LongMuEL, which can represent the long descriptive text of candidate entities and integrate structured text from candidate entity knowledge bases. In the long text embedding module, we use multiple attention modules and weight pooling for all truncated text. When obtaining the embedding of structured text, we adopt two self-supervised tasks to pre-train the pre-trained model and generate negative examples through negative sampling. We demonstrate that pre-training the model with two self-supervised tasks results in better embedding effects for structured data. Finally, we fuse the embedding vectors generated from the two data types to calculate the ranking of candidate entities. LongMuEL is a knowledge graph completion model adapted to existing data features, and through ablation experiments, we verify the effectiveness of each part of LongMuEL.

articleTitle: Sound-based Mosquito Classification via Featurization and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases impact over 3 billion people globally, causing more than 600,000 deaths each year. Precise mosquito species identification is crucial for outbreak prediction but is limited by manual, subjective methods requiring specialized skills and equipment, hindering scalability. Climate change exacerbates this by altering habitats. Citizen science, leveraging smartphone-captured mosquito sounds, offers an alternative option for scalable identification and tracking. Low-cost identification techniques can enable broad deployment in sensors and other inexpensive devices for non-invasive mosquito tracking in remote areas, reducing human disease exposure. Our work investigates sound featurization and machine learning for non-invasive mosquito type identification. Using a dataset of 200 smartphone-recorded mosquitoes, sound featurization, and Random Forest classification, we show that two common breeds (Anopheles and Culiseta) can be distinguished with over 98% accuracy, and that Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) Featurization outperforms other methods (spectrograms and spectrogram featurization) for this 2-class problem but underperforms in distinguishing between Anopheles variants.

articleTitle: Optimizing University Teachers Learning Progress: Evolving Study Efficiency with Artificial Intelligence Agent
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This paper explores using the COZE AI Agent platform to optimize university teachers’ learning progress and study efficiency. Key requirements like personalized learning paths, technology integration, and pedagogical innovation are identified. Testing evaluates the AI agent’s performance in generating tailored professional development recommendations. Results demonstrate improved study efficiency and professional growth through accurate, relevant advice. Limitations and prospects, including continuous feedback loops and data analysis, are discussed, highlighting AI agents’ potential to revolutionize professional development in higher education.

articleTitle: Enhancing Credit Card Fraud Detection Through Adaptive Model Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Credit card fraud remains a persistent threat in electronic transactions, driving ongoing advancements in fraud detection methodologies. We proposed an innovative method to fortify credit card fraud check systems through adaptive model optimization. We first start by addressing the inherent challenges of accurately defining fraud and managing imbalanced datasets, stressing the necessity for dynamic solutions to adapt to evolving fraud patterns. Our methodology leverages historical credit card transaction data to construct a flexible predictive model capable of discerning fraudulent activities while minimizing false classifications. By prioritizing the maximization of recall alongside controlling the false positive rate, our approach ensures robust fraud detection capabilities without sacrificing precision. Furthermore, we introduce novel techniques for feature analysis and preprocessing in the absence of comprehensive metadata, facilitating deeper insights into transaction characteristics. Through empirical validation on real-world datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our adaptive model optimization framework in improving fraud detection accuracy and scalability. By implementing logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost with the SMOTE method, our approach empowers businesses with proactive fraud prevention measures, safeguarding financial assets, and bolstering consumer trust in electronic payment systems.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) pose a significant threat to global public health, affecting individuals across various age groups. Factors such as cholesterol levels, smoking, alcohol consumption, and physical inactivity contribute to their onset and progression. Enhancing our understanding of CVD etiology and informing targeted interventions for disease prevention and management remains a critical challenge. In this study, we address the task of predicting the likelihood of individuals developing CVDs using machine learning techniques. Specifically, we explore three approaches: the k-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm, logistic regression, and the random forest algorithm. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset sourced from Kaggle, encompassing 11 relevant factors, we conduct a series of experiments to identify the most influential predictors of CVDs. Our analysis aims not only to forecast disease occurrence but also to elucidate the primary determinants contributing to its manifestation. Through comparative analysis of the three methodologies, we demonstrate that the random forest algorithm exhibits superior performance in terms of predictive accuracy. This research represents a significant step towards leveraging machine learning techniques to enhance our understanding of CVD dynamics and inform targeted interventions for disease prevention and management.

articleTitle: SecureNet: A Comparative Study of DeBERTa and Large Language Models for Phishing Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Phishing, whether through email, SMS, or malicious websites, poses a major threat to organizations by using social engineering to trick users into revealing sensitive information. This not only compromises company’s data security but also incurs significant financial losses. In this paper, we investigate whether the remarkable performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) can be leveraged for particular task like text classification, particularly detecting malicious content and compare its results with state-of-the-art Deberta V3 (DeBERTa using ELECTRA-Style Pre-Training with Gradient-Disentangled Embedding Sharing) model. We systematically assess the potential and limitations of both the approaches using comprehensive public datasets comprising diverse data sources such as email, HTML, URL, SMS, and synthetic data generation. Additionally, we demonstrate how LLMs can generate convincing phishing emails, making it harder to spot scams and evaluate the performance of both models in this context. Our study delves further into the challenges encountered by DeBERTa V3 during its training phases, fine-tuning methodology and transfer learning processes. Similarly, we examine the challenges associated with LLMs and assess their respective performance. Among our experimental approaches, the transformer-based DeBERTa method emerged as the most effective, achieving a test dataset (HuggingFace phishing dataset) recall (sensitivity) of 95.17% closely followed by GPT-4 providing a recall of 91.04%. We performed additional experiments with other datasets on the trained DeBERTa V3 model and LLMs like GPT 4 and Gemini 1.5. Based on our findings, we provide valuable insights into the effectiveness and robustness of these advanced language models, offering a detailed comparative analysis that can inform future research efforts in strengthening cybersecurity measures for detecting and mitigating phishing threats.

articleTitle: Overcoming the Challenges of Large Language Models: Introducing a Novel Proposition for Synthetic Data Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The market debut of ChatGPT gave rise to the development and deployment of various other Large Language Models (LLMs) that achieve state-of-the-art performance across various tasks. The growing popularity of these models has captivated some to attempt to construct or enhance their own LLM. We must be aware of the significant problems that already exist and that we might face along the way. This paper aims to identify and investigate the main challenges in this field, provide existing solutions, and propose novel approaches to mitigate them. A unique Truth-Table proposition for validating synthetic data is presented examining two models, along with a bidirectional knowledge graph-based solution for curing the reverse curse problem, data generation strategies, domain adaptation methods, and the use of a custom dataset to address model hallucinations. The methodology and findings of this study provide valuable insights for users, researchers, and industry experts who are interested in LLMs. It serves as a reference for future research on current models, refining models or developing domain-specific ones.

articleTitle: Exploring on Human Pose Estimation from the Perspective of Feature Map Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: In the field of computer vision, accurately recognising the position of human keypoints in complex scenes plays an important role in understanding human pose.Factors such as mutual occlusion of human bodies, low illumination, and blurring make human key point feature extraction still a challenging problem.For convolutional neural networks, extracting image features is the key to achieve the task goal, and making full use of contextual information for multi-scale feature fusion of feature maps is undoubtedly a useful attempt.In this study, a feature fusion network, FusionPoseNet, is constructed from the perspective of feature maps to make full use of the spatial and semantic information embedded in feature maps at different scales, to enhance the interaction capability between the information, and to explore the effect of mutual fusion between feature maps on accurately identifying the key points of the human skeleton. In addition, this paper also carries out a triage fusion process on the feature map as a way to reduce the number of network parameters and improve the speed of model inference.In this paper, we conduct experiments on the COCO dataset. The experimental results show that our method has higher accuracy on the COCO dataset relative to the typical SimpleBaseline algorithm, and at the same time the amount of computation is reduced dramatically (by 21%), which is a good improvement for solving the problem of inaccurate identification of keypoints due to the complex background.

articleTitle: Enhancing Student Retention in Higher Education: A Fuzzy Logic Approach to Prescriptive Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Prescriptive analytics is used in this study to evaluate the need for intervention support programs that target students at risk of dropping out. It makes use of a fuzzy logic-based algorithm with five identified linguistic variables, which arose from a previous study that sought to establish the major factors affecting student dropout risk and predict such risks based on given input variables. For accuracy, these variables were fuzzified and converted into multiple categories with different levels of membership through the use of triangular and trapezoidal membership functions. In developing the knowledge base, 32 fuzzy rules were established to enable the generation of effective outputs that identify appropriate intervention programs. Finally, the Centroid formula (or Centroid of Gravity) was employed in identifying a specific intervention program.

articleTitle: Robust and Efficient Outlier Detection Algorithm Based on Linear Neighborhood Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Outlier detection aims to identify observations significantly deviating from the norm in a dataset. Existing detection methods face challenges in setting thresholds and tuning parameters. We introduce a novel Linear Neighborhood Sequence (LNS), insensitive to the parameter k, where objects share an outlier score. Moreover, we design an adaptive thresholding to partition anomaly sequences and capture outliers based on LNS properties. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the robustness of our LNS outlier detector to parameter k and its effectiveness in outlier detection. Moreover, our method requires a significantly lower valid k value compared to similar kNN-based algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhanced Channel-Temporal Transformer with Neural Architecture Search For Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting (MTSF) has been given attention for a long time in practical scenarios such as energy usage, traffic patterns and weather prediction. Transformer-based models have been proven successful in NLP and Computer Vision due to the ability of the self-attention mechanism that can csapture long term dependencies. Recently, transformer-based models are starting to be adopted in MTSF to capture both the temporal dependencies and channel dependencies. As there is an increasing variety of attention mechanisms in MTSF while each mechanism has varied performance on different dataset, it becomes crucial to determine the most optimal mechanism for a given dataset. The purpose of this research is to build a framework that searches for the most optimal attention mechanisms for learning the deep features of the given MTS dataset and study its effectiveness. Generic transformer architecture for MTSF is composed of an embedding layer, an encoder made up of both temporal layer and channel layer, and the decoder. Optuna Hyperparameter Optimization framework is proposed to find the best attention mechanisms for the temporal and channel layer in the encoder. The search space is the mixture of attention mechanisms from several high-performing MTSF transformer architectures such as CARD, Convolutional Triplet Attention and Lightweight Temporal Self Attention. The heterogeneous transformer formed with the different attention mechanisms will be evaluated on the real-world MTS datasets against the standalone architectures. This is to deduce whether combining different attention mechanisms is more effective.

articleTitle: GP-PAIL: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning in Massive-Agent Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms are unsuitable for massive-agent environments where the problems of credit allocation, dense reward function design and stage course design become pronounced. Since massive-agent environments can only give sparse rewards to the agents, these algorithms face difficulty in learning effective actions. While specially designed dense reward functions can help the agents to obtain more reward signals, the algorithms face a trade-off between convergence speed and generalization ability. Although a hand-crafted reward function can provide frequent feedback that accelerates the learning of the agents, excessively detailed rewards may cause the agents to focus on short-term rewards and overlook long-term goals, resulting in a sub-optimal strategy. To address this, we propose GP-PAIL (Generative Pixel-to-Pixel Adversarial Imitation Learning), a novel generative adversarial imitation learning algorithm that uses a pixel-to-pixel policy structure for centralized control. It mitigates the issues of fixed behavioral patterns and credit allocation inherent in the specially designed of dense reward functions and staged curricula, enhancing imitation learning in massive-agent environments. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of GP-PAIL, with a 92% win rate compared to the best12 algorithm. Furthermore, in terms of early skill learning speed, it improves nearly 3.25 times faster on number of episodes compared to the current state-of-the-art best32 algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhancing Compressive Strength Prediction in Recycled Aggregate Concrete Using XGBoost Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The accurate prediction of compressive strength in recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) presents a significant challenge due to its heterogeneous nature. This study focuses on enhancing the predictive performance and interpretability of the XGBoost, a powerful machine-learning algorithm, for compressive strength prediction in RAC. Using GridSearchCV, hyperparameter optimization was conducted to refine the model’s parameters. Additionally, SHAP analysis was employed to provide insights into the global and local interpretations of the model. The results demonstrate significant improvements in predictive accuracy, with the tuned XGBoost model achieving higher $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ scores compared to the default model. Furthermore, reductions in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) were observed, indicating enhanced precision in predicting compressive strength values. The SHAP analyses reveal influential features impacting RAC strength, highlighting the significance of cement, water, sand, and recycled aggregate water absorption in predicting RAC compressive strength. These findings not only contribute to advancing predictive modeling techniques in concrete engineering but also highlight the efficacy of GridSearchCV in optimizing the performance of machine learning models for heterogeneous materials like RAC.

articleTitle: Hybridized Shield: A Framework for Backdoor Detection in Secure Federated Learning Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: In the context of Federated Learning, the vulnerability to backdoor attacks poses a significant threat to the integrity and reliability of distributed learning systems. This research introduces a novel defense framework, the” Hybridized Shield,” designed to safeguard Federated Learning environments robustly against such insidious threats. The proposed mechanism integrates Oblivious Random Grouping, Partial Parameter Disclosure, and differential outlier analysis, forming a comprehensive defense strategy that addresses the unique challenges of Federated Learning’s decentralized and collaborative nature. The results reveal a significant improvement in the resilience of Federated Learning systems against backdoor attacks. Specifically, the proposed method maintains high accuracy on clean data ($\mathbf{9 7. 9 2 \%}$ on MNIST and CIFAR-10) while significantly reducing the effectiveness of poisoned data attacks to a mere $\mathbf{1 0. 1 1 \%}$ accuracy, compared to the baseline Federated Learning model without defense mechanisms, which showed a $100 \%$ accuracy on poisoned data and an $18.56 \%$ attack success rate. These findings underscore the efficacy of the” Hybridized Shield” in preserving the integrity and security of Federated Learning systems, thereby contributing to the advancement of secure and reliable distributed machine learning methodologies.

articleTitle: A Study on Investment Strategies Utilizing Multi-Factor Analysis Based on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of big data technology, there is an increasing interest in utilizing big data in investment strategies. This study focuses on the research of a multi-factor investment strategy based on big data analysis. The objective is to identify and incorporate multiple factors that have a significant impact on stock performance. The research adopts a comprehensive approach by collecting and analyzing a large amount of financial and non-financial data. Various factors such as financial ratios, market sentiment, news sentiment, and macroeconomic indicators are considered. Machine learning algorithms are applied to process and analyze the data, enabling the identification of key factors that drive stock prices. The findings suggest that a multi-factor investment strategy based on big data analysis can outperform traditional strategies. By incorporating a wide range of factors, the strategy provides a more comprehensive view of the market and reduces reliance on individual factors. Additionally, the research demonstrates the importance of continuous data collection and analysis to adapt to changing market conditions. This study focuses on the constituents of the CSI300 Index designs indicators from three aspects: profitability, valuation, and growth, to verify their relationship with stock returns. A multi-factor stock selection model is constructed by incorporating technical indicators. Empirical results show that the multi-factor model portfolio outperforms the CSI300 Index in both bear and bull markets, generating excess returns. Moreover, the combination model that includes both financial indicators and technical indicators performs better than the model that solely relies on financial indicators.

articleTitle: From Big Data to Massive Data: Towards a Massive Data Storage Solution for the Internet of Senses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The increased maturity of current digitalization techniques expands the scope of practical deployments in various fields, including the precipitation of “digital biology” as a novel and highly important new field of research. This research area specializes in the convergence of various digital technologies and investigations into biology, offering the possibility to produce new comprehension of and applications for living systems by leveraging frameworks of digital technology. The enhanced scope of current capacities in computation facilitates simulated models of multifaceted biological artefacts and novel ways to gather, analyze, and interpret data, moving far beyond the primitive scope of legacy solutions in this field. This paper explores potential “massive data” databases, developing a conceptual model to move beyond the existing “big data” paradigm.

articleTitle: Classroom Activity Detection from Audio-Text Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Classroom Activity Detection (CAD) focuses on accurately determining who is speaking—whether it’s a teacher, a student, or during a classroom discussion—and recording the length and total amount of individual speech in the classroom. Most existing models addressing the CAD problem only use audio information, which does not suffice for some real classroom scenarios. Because the real classroom is an open environment and less analysis of activities in this environment, it is a challenge to extract audio function and build a data set. Additionally, the teacher’s voice may be very similar to that of some students. Therefore, to fully leverage the multimodal information available in classrooms, this paper proposes a multimodal classroom activity detection model. This model improves the audio feature extraction network and uses the attention mechanism to integrate the key points of text information into audio information. Compared to other models, our model achieves significant improvements on our established classroom dataset, EQclass.

articleTitle: TCAE-DL-RGCN Based Detection of Twitter Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Twitter bot detection is a challenging task that has received widespread attention in the field of social security. Detection of Twitter bots using graph neural networks has been widely used, graph neural networks are prone to over-smoothing phenomenon affecting the model accuracy when extracting features from the data so the number of network layers is usually small and there is insufficient feature extraction when extracting features from the data. To address the above challenges, our research proposes the TCAE-DL-RGCN model, which fuses the RGCN features extracted by the attention mechanism of controlled attention temperature with the RGCN extracted features to prevent over-smoothing and to improve the feature expression capability and model accuracy. Our extensive experiments on the public Twitter robot detection dataset Twibot-20 show that TCAE-DL-RGCN achieves optimal performance.

articleTitle: An Efficient Privacy-Preserving Asynchronous Federated Approach for Intelligent Decision Making in Equipment Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative training of a high-quality global model across multiple participants without sharing raw local data. Its advantages, such as decentralization, data isolation, and high computational performance, have made it a popular research direction in various fields. However, federated learning faces privacy risks during model parameter transmission. Additionally, reducing communication overhead and computational resource consumption while ensuring data privacy protection remains a critical challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes an efficient privacy-preserving asynchronous federated learning method tailored for equipment maintenance scenarios. Leveraging asynchronous federated learning techniques, this method enables efficient collaborative training among multiple participants. It also employs homomorphic encryption to protect local data information. By utilizing time-series models, we construct a predictive model for equipment spare parts consumption, providing valuable insights for intelligent maintenance decision-making. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method has faster convergence. More importantly, the root mean square error decreases by at least 0.004, the mean square error decreases by at least 0.024, and the relative error decreases by at least 0.008 compared to the baseline.

articleTitle: A Literature Knowledge Discovery Model Based on Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: This study developed a literature knowledge discovery model based on graph neural network and applied it in the field of potential drug discovery for Covid-19. The study utilized the Therapeutic Target Database (TTD) to construct a network of drug-target-disease relationships, and employed an association prediction method using graph convolutional neural network to discover potential connections between drugs and new coronavirus targets. A total of 5,358 “intermediary target-candidate drug” pairs were identified, revealing 1,624 potential relationships, ultimately leading to the identification of 50 potential new coronavirus treatment drugs. Subsequent literature review revealed that 28 of these drugs are currently undergoing clinical validation and have shown promising therapeutic effects against COVID-19. Additionally, 5 drugs were identified through various bioinformatics methods, while the remaining drugs have not yet been reported. The results of this research demonstrate that the literature knowledge discovery model based on graph neural networks can effectively unveil valuable insights from existing literature and facilitate the discovery of drugs with potential therapeutic benefits for COVID-19.

articleTitle: Integrating Mechanistic Knowledge with Deep Learning Models for Wellbore Integrity Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: As global oil resources gradually deplete, the development of deepwater oil and gas resources becomes particularly important. However, the exploitation of deepwater oil and gas resources is characterized by high technology, high investment, and high risk, especially in terms of production safety. This study aims to accurately predict wellbore annular pressure by analyzing the time series of wellbore production data using advanced Transformer models and a multi-scale mechanism. By incorporating a multi-scale mechanism, the model can pay attention to both short-term subtle changes and long-term trend changes. Experimental results show that compared to traditional LSTM models and Transformer, our Multi-Scale Transformer model demonstrates advantages in prediction accuracy and the ability to handle long sequence data. This will contribute to enhancing the safety and economic efficiency of deepwater oil and gas development.

articleTitle: Enhanced Intrusion Detection in Big Data Systems: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Robust intrusion detection systems (IDS) are critical in big data environments due to the growing volume and complexity of network traffic, as they protect against cyberattacks. Conventional signature-based intrusion detection systems have difficulty keeping up with new attack techniques. In large data network security, machine learning and deep learning methods are viable substitutes for anomaly detection. To attain better performance on big data network traffic datasets, this study suggests a unique deep learning-based intrusion detection system (IDS) that makes use of capsule networks, bi-directional LSTMs (BiLSTMs), and embedding layers. We create a deep learning model for feature extraction and pattern detection from network traffic data by combining an embedding layer, a capsule layer, and a BiLSTM layer. To test the model’s efficacy in intrusion detection, two benchmark datasets UNSW-NB15 and an IoT dataset are used. With a test accuracy of 99.99% on the UNSWNB15 dataset, the suggested model performs remarkably well on both datasets. This shows the model’s greater capacity to detect anomalies and possible intrusions within big data network traffic, surpassing the accuracy reported in earlier studies. The results demonstrate how well the suggested deep learning architecture for big data intrusion detection works. Due to its excellent accuracy and generalizability over a wide range of datasets, the model has practical applications in protecting big data networks from cyberattacks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Personal Protective Equipment Compliance and Usage Accuracy on Construction Sites through YOLOv7 Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Frequent monitoring of adherence to personal protective equipment is crucial on construction sites to protect workers’ health and reduce potential risks in the workplace. Still, manually verifying the use of PPE during toolbox meetings is a lengthy process, complex, and susceptible to human errors. To enhance operational efficiency, mitigate risks, and ensure compliance with construction regulations, this study proposes utilizing artificial intelligence to detect PPE presence and its proper usage. The research focuses on developing a YOLOv7 model along with a web application for management monitoring and notification. The testing result shows that using the trained model with a training accuracy of $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$, the proposed system achieved high detection efficiency on personal protective equipment compliance and usage. Automating the detection and monitoring process allows the system to decrease the need for manual supervision, thus freeing resources for other tasks. Furthermore, it takes a proactive approach to addressing compliance issues, enhancing safety protocols, and reducing the chances of accidents and injuries.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Model for the Detection of Bacterial Wilt and Crown Rot diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: With the digital revolution, thanks to data already prepared or collected via sensors - a camera, for example with transmission systems, computer data constitutes a resource of inestimable value. Access to a large amount of data and the development of new algorithms have led to major breakthroughs in the field of Artificial Intelligence in recent years. In this paper, accurate identification of plant diseases is crucial for establishing effective crop protection systems. Traditional methods based on visual observation present significant biases. Based on digital data collected in the agriculture sector, this study proposes a deep learning model for the automatic detection of bacterial wilt and crown rot in Solanum macrocarpon vegetable locally called “gboma”. The methodology is based on the processing of images of symptomatic leaves collected at the Laboratoire de Défense des Cultures (LADC) of the Institut National de la Recherche Agricole du Bénin (INRAB). The preprocessed images are classified by a convolutional neural network developed with Keras based on the VGG16 architecture. On a total of 586 training images, the model achieved $\mathbf{9 8. 3 \%}$ accuracy on training and $\mathbf{9 7. 1 \%}$ on cross-validation. These promising results pave the way for the deployment of an automated field diagnostic tool for effective and sustainable protection of gboma crops.

articleTitle: RoD2M: Robust Deep Multi-modal Multi-label Model for Mobile App Security Rating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: As the number of mobile internet users continues to expand, the number of apps is increasing, which involves various app security issues. It is crucial to generate a comprehensive rating for mobile applications based on various security issues. Currently, there is limited research on comprehensive rating of mobile applications, leading to a one-sided rating of applications. To solve these problems, we propose a Robust Deep Multi-modal Multi-label Model (RoD2M). Firstly, we innovatively use multimodal security data to better rate mobile applications. Then, we propose an attention-based autoencoder to make the model more robust and extract key data representations. Finally, we propose a modal fusion degree block and a modal contribution degree block, so that the model can also better cope with label imbalance and the problem of different modalities contributing differently to different labels. The results on real datasets also demonstrate the superiority and effectiveness of our model (e.g. reaching 0.928 accuracy and 0.949 micro-f1).

articleTitle: Grassland Bareness Detection Algorithm Based on CST-YOLO Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: With the increasing pursuit of quality of life, community green space management has become increasingly important. Existing large-scale green space detection methods primarily rely on remote sensing satellites and deep learning to extract features and determine the coverage and growth status of green spaces. These methods often have long judgment cycles and are suited for large areas, making them unsuitable for the real-time and small-area detection needs of communities. This paper addresses the issue of abnormal growth in community green spaces by proposing an improved CST-YOLO algorithm to effectively detect such abnormalities. The algorithm incorporates three core innovations: Firstly, considering the limited number of samples in current research, a dedicated dataset containing 4,000 images of patchy bald and withered green spaces was constructed. Secondly, a global information module was added to the backbone network to more effectively integrate global and detailed features of the images. Finally, a hybrid attention mechanism combining spatial and channel attention was introduced into the neck network, and the loss function was improved to adaptively refine the features of the input feature map. This enhancement strengthens the features of key target areas and improves detection accuracy.Ablation and comparative experimental results show that this model performs excellently in feature fusion capabilities, providing auxiliary judgment for community manual management and better meeting the practical needs of community environmental management.

articleTitle: Predicting Electrical Vehicle Charging Patterns at Public Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: As electrical vehicle (EV) technologies become mature, there is a rapid growth in public charging infrastructures. With public charging stations, an accurate prediction of local charging demand can enable many applications, such as dynamic charging allocations, optimizations of power grid operations, and proactive planning for EV users. However, charging demand prediction is a challenging problem, because it is usually affected by the diverse behaviors exhibited by different user groups. In this paper, we explore a data-driven approach to leverage historical charging records for the prediction of future charging demand. We develop a predictive model that distinguishes between the behaviors of both registered long-term users and unregistered short-term users. Utilizing a real-world dataset of 28053 records over 798 days at multiple locations, we employ several supervised learning algorithms to evaluate the performances of our models. Our evaluation results demonstrate that our model, enhanced with the XGBoost, significantly outperforms alternative solutions. It achieves a reduction in prediction error up to 40.8% at the finest time granularity (15-minute interval).

articleTitle: Tree Barriers and Power Lines Segmentation from Point Clouds Based on Improved Point Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The overgrowth of trees along power lines poses a significant threat to the safe operation of power transmission systems. Accurate detection and removal of trees barriers is crucial for ensuring grid reliability. While the advanced Visual Transformer (ViT) model, Point Transformer, has shown promising results in this domain, there is still room for improvement in terms of inference speed and segmentation accuracy. ResMLP, a feedforward network designed for image classification, offers data-efficient training and greater stability than ViT. Inspired by these advancements, we design a novel module, ResBlock, which integrates the data-efficient ResMLP network into the 3D domain. This forms the foundation of our PointRes model, which builds upon the core structure of Point Transformer while incorporating lightweight and stable modules. Experimental results show that the model we proposed enjoys a smaller quantity of parameters, but a better performance, reaching a 71.6% Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) on the S3DIS dataset. We further evaluate PointRes on the DALES dataset, demonstrating its ability to identify tree barriers. Additionally, we propose a method for generating detailed tree barrier reports. PointRes represents a novel approach that competes effectively in segmenting tree barriers and power lines.

articleTitle: Research Trends in Application of Artificial Intelligence in Alzheimer’s Disease: Bibliometric and Visualization Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: The remarkable performance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the diagnosis and prediction of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) has attracted considerable attention in recent years. This study intends to outline the development trends and research focus in the AI-Alzheimer field. The VOSviewer and bibliometrix R software package are employed for bibliometrics and visualization analysis of literature obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection database. There are 5,991 affiliations from 104 countries/regions that published 5,675 articles in this field by 2023. Results demonstrate that the number of AIAlzheimer-related publications has experienced slow progress for over twenty years before entering a period of exponential growth in 2016. The United States and China, contributing over 54% of the publications, stand out as leaders in technological innovation and international cooperation. The clustering analysis of keywords indicates that the major research domains are the utilization of machine learning and deep learning algorithms for AD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) classification, early diagnosis of disease, and drug discovery. Generative adversarial networks (GANs), transfer learning, and Transformers are the emerging AI algorithms applied in the field of Alzheimer’s research, which also represent promising directions for future investigation. The findings provide a comprehensive summary of the AI-Alzheimer field and identify research frontiers, offering valuable references for scholars.

articleTitle: The Influence Mechanism of Smart Wearable Health Technologies User Technology Adoption Intention: Based on the Mediating Role of User Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: With the rapid enhancement of intelligent technological capabilities, intelligent products are increasingly intervening in the user consumption process, which may challenge the inherent cognition and needs of users and lead to significant negative impacts. Therefore, this study focuses on the research domain of Smart wearable health technologies (SWHTs), starting from the perspective of user engagement, to explore the mechanism of the impact of different dimensions of intelligent technology interaction perception on users’ willingness to adopt the technology. The study uses partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) for research validation, and the results indicate that the perceived personalization, responsiveness, and controllability of SWHTs have a positive impact on users’ willingness to adopt the technology, while user engagement plays a mediating role.
